 Eastern Rajasthan may see strong winds, rain and thunderstorms over next two days: IMD
 Written By ZeeBiz WebTeam Published: 8:57 PM, Oct 29, 2026 | Updated: 8:58 PM, Oct 29, 2026 Meanwhile, Cyclone Arnab, which originated over the Bay of Bengal, has also affected parts of Chhattisgarh, bringing intermittent rainfall and strong winds over the past two days. Strong winds have flattened standing paddy in several fields. | ChatGPT generated/Representative Image Several parts of eastern Rajasthan are likely to witness thunderstorms, strong winds and light to moderate rainfall till October 30 due to changes in weather systems over northwestern and central India, IMD Jaipur Director Radheshyam Sharma said.
 Sharma said the cyclonic storm that developed over the Bay of Bengal has weakened into a well-marked low-pressure area and is currently lying over northern Chhattisgarh and adjoining parts of Odisha. The system is expected to weaken further as it moves northward.
 At the same time, a fresh western disturbance has become active over northwest India and nearby regions, while an induced cyclonic circulation has developed over Punjab and adjoining areas.
 "Due to the combined effect of these systems, the sky will remain cloudy across many parts of eastern Rajasthan today," Sharma told ANI.
 He added that the weather conditions were expected to persist until October 30, with thunderstorms, strong winds and light to moderate rainfall likely in several areas.
 "The impact is expected to be most significant in the Jaipur and Bharatpur divisions, as well as several parts of the Ajmer division. Parts of the Udaipur and Kota divisions may also experience thunderstorms accompanied by strong winds," Sharma said.
 Cyclone Arnab damages paddy crops 
 Meanwhile, Cyclone Arnab , which originated over the Bay of Bengal, has also affected parts of Chhattisgarh, bringing intermittent rainfall and strong winds over the past two days.
 The impact has been reported across Bastar, Raipur, Bilaspur and Surguja divisions, where farmers said ripe paddy crops ready for harvesting have suffered damage.
 Strong winds have flattened standing paddy in several fields, while waterlogging caused by the rain has added to concerns over further crop losses.
 Farmers said strong winds had flattened standing paddy plants, while waterlogging in several fields had increased the risk of further crop damage. They said they had borrowed money to arrange seeds, fertilisers and other agricultural inputs, and the loss of their ready-to-harvest crop had left them uncertain about repaying their loans and managing household expenses.
 Indian Coast Guard conducts airlift operation 
 As Cyclone Arnab continues to impact the eastern coast of India, the Indian Coast Guard (ICG) Regional Headquarters (North East) has placed its air and surface assets on high alert to execute critical Search and Rescue (SAR) alongside Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) missions. ICG aviation assets in the region remain on standby for round-the-clock aerial surveillance, emergency evacuations, and air-dropping essential relief materials to isolated communities.
 ​In response to a distress call received from the Ganjam District Administration on the morning of October 29, 2026, the Coast Guard Air Enclave, Bhubaneswar, swiftly scrambled an ALH Mk-III helicopter despite severe weather conditions.
 Navigating challenging elements, the aircrew pinpointed the heavily inundated Public Health Centre (PHC) in Jagmohan, where individuals were stranded due to post-storm floodwaters. Executing a precision hover over the submerged area, the crew successfully winched six individuals, including two women, two children, and one elderly person, to safety. The rescued personnel were airlifted and safely transferred to the Community Health Centre (CHC) in Dharakote.
